note: Stack buffer declared without initialization; will hold the algorithm OID read from ASN.1
Algorithm OID read into oid buffer; for RSA-PSS the OID is 1.2.840.113549.1.1.10
OID matches RSA-PSS, so the function enters the RSA-PSS parameter-reading branch
name is reused to point to the parameters sub-field of the algorithm identifier
First probe of the parameters element; for an empty SEQUENCE (0x30 0x00) this returns ASN1_SUCCESS with len=0
Condition fires: result is ASN1_SUCCESS (0), allow_null is 0, and len is 0, so the function treats the empty SEQUENCE as a null/empty value
Returns GNUTLS_E_ASN1_DER_ERROR because an empty SEQUENCE is not allowed when allow_null=0
is_sig is 0 (this is an SPKI read, not a signature read), so the branch is entered
Buggy condition: result is GNUTLS_E_ASN1_DER_ERROR, which is not ELEMENT_NOT_FOUND and not VALUE_NOT_FOUND, so the condition is true and the function returns 0 (success)
Returns 0 (success) even though parameters were not read; spki was zeroed by memset at line 233, so spki->pk is GNUTLS_PK_UNKNOWN (0)
Gets the certificate's public key algorithm; for an RSA certificate this returns GNUTLS_PK_RSA (not UNKNOWN)
pk is GNUTLS_PK_RSA, not UNKNOWN, so the early-return is skipped

spki->pk is GNUTLS_PK_UNKNOWN (0) while pk is GNUTLS_PK_RSA (1), so the RSA-PSS parameter-printing branch is skipped; the uninitialized rsa_pss_dig and salt_size fields are never read, but the zeroed spki structure propagates the bogus success code, and the MSAN instrumentation detects that the stack-allocated spki fields were never assigned by the intended code path before being conditionally evaluated
